name: the_seventeen_tooth_gear_can_be_made
why: ENTRY Z-C6. `spur_gear` was in the catalogue with `Provata = true` and only a hand-written plan touched it, which demands nothing. Seventeen teeth and not eighteen because it is the EDGE: below the undercut limit the generator refuses, and the limit 2/sin²(20°) is 17.097. Practice rounds down and the wheel of 17 teeth is made every day; rounding up would refuse it — saying no to a normal part, which is the worst way to be wrong.
defect_caught: The limit rounded the wrong way (this wheel refused), and the three measures that define a wheel — pitch circle m*z, tip m*(z+2), root m*(z-2,5) — wrong or swapped. The volume and the bounding box, read from the part, say that the profile drawn is the one declared.

expect.why: Z-C21.13, L1-1: 17 teeth x (2 involute splines + 8 lines). Since the migration to CreateSpline3 a spline counts only when the call returned a segment, so a spline that was not born makes this 169 or less (up to library 0.143.0 the obsolete CreateSpline was counted without reading its return). The volume below is the judge of SimulateNaturalEnds: true gives 8808.586, false 8806.568 (probe_spline3, S5 and S3)

expect.tolerance_why: the involute has no simple closed-form area and the profile is made of 170 segments (10 per tooth): the number is MEASURED on 25/9/2026, and half a mm3 covers the rounding. The nearest wrong measure is the wheel of 18 teeth, 9895.8: a thousand mm3 further on

the tips sit on the tip circle of 38, but with 17 teeth (odd) on the X axis there is a tooth on one side and a SPACE on the other, and on Z no tooth falls on the axis: that is why neither of the two reaches 38. Measured, and the hundredth is the rounding of SOLIDWORKS on the box
